teenKit.tldr: National drug laws fail because politicians write borders and statutes, but molecules only respond to atomic geometry at the one-angstrom scale. This episode maps how real-world policies in Uruguay, Canada, and Colombia collide with exact protein shapes.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding the physical shape of molecules inside our brains changes how we look at addiction, public health laws, and why simple military crackdowns never work.
keyTakeaways: Molecules like cocaine and methamphetamine do not read government statutes or respect international borders.
Uruguay, Canada, and British Columbia have run massive real-world policy experiments ranging from biometric state pharmacies to supervised injection sites like Vancouver's Insite.
Drug interaction comes down to precise atomic geometry, such as the dopamine transporter binding a bulky 10.23-angstrom cocaine molecule versus a sleek 6.64-angstrom synthetic methamphetamine.
